title: Biographical details; parents' background
description: Cathy Naugle records Mary Elizabeth Avery's maiden name Jasper, her 1917 birth in the now-vanished town of Roseberry, Idaho, and her address. Avery then gives details about her mother Mary Etta Cole, born in Texas, and works out her parents' birth and death dates.

title: Father's family ferry; thirteenth child; sister's book
description: Avery recounts that her father John Marrel Jasper was born beside his family's ferry at Buttermilk Slew on the Snake River near Weiser, and later farmed and served as postmaster near Roseberry. She explains she is the youngest of thirteen children, with grandchildren older than herself, and shows Naugle a memoir, My Roseberry, written by her sister Cynthia Pottinger.

title: Marriage to Clyde Avery; move to Lewiston; children
description: Avery tells of marrying Clyde L. Avery, also born in Roseberry, in Cascade, and moving to Lewiston where he worked his way up to co-ownership of Star Motor Freight. She names their two children, Jasper, a mechanical engineering instructor at the University of Idaho, and Nancy Lee Fish, who works part-time at a newspaper near North Bend, Washington.

title: Schooling; city clerk career; hobbies
description: Avery describes her high school schooling in Donnelly and her nearly thirty years as City Clerk-Treasurer, a job she entered through bookkeeping at Star Motor Freight in Orofino and which has grown more specialized over time. She also mentions crocheting, collecting brass and Hummel figurines, and the council and planning meetings that occupy her evenings.

title: Rural versus urban life; family size; schooling and marriage expectations
description: Avery explains her preference for small-town life, recalling that her childhood community had no electricity until 1934, and discusses why her generation had smaller families than their parents. She reflects on her siblings' schooling, her reasons for marrying, and her daughter's unfinished college degree.

title: Childbirth; Depression and war years; keeping house
description: Avery recalls bearing one child in a Lewiston hospital and another at a neighbor's home, and having some sex education in school. She describes starting married life on thirty dollars a week during the Depression, Clyde's essential-industry exemption in World War II, and keeping house for her father after her mother's death.

title: Widowhood plans; marriage partnership; family finances
description: Avery considers how she would manage if her husband died, noting insurance and her ability to keep working. She credits Clyde's support of her career for their congenial marriage, describes their shared recreation, and laughs about managing the family bookkeeping and talking him into new ventures.

title: Home building; Decision making
description: Mary Elizabeth Avery recounts the surprise of her husband discovering plans to build apartments through a misplaced cap. She also discusses the evolution of decision-making in her marriage.

title: Reading habits; Television and entertainment
description: Avery talks about the magazines and books she and her husband enjoy, her disinterest in women's magazines, and their limited TV watching.

title: Music preferences; Square dancing
description: She describes her family's music preferences and recalls square-dancing in her youth, including local dances known as 'Kitchen sweats.'

title: Church attendance; Household management
description: Avery discusses her religious background, her independent management of household affairs, and contrasts her approach with other women.

title: Marriage dynamics; Advice for women
description: She reflects on her long marriage, personal growth, and offers advice to women about maintaining independence.

title: Family background; Conclusion
description: Avery discusses her husband's family background, the presence of divorce in her own family, and the interview concludes.
